title: Meghna Gulzar on Irrfan Khan: 'Everything He Did, He Made Me Look Good'
excerpt: Speaking to The Indian Express's Expresso series ahead of Daayra's September 18 release, the Raazi and Talvar director reflected on Irrfan Khan, Vicky Kaushal and Deepika Padukone — and said she still doesn't know which side of Talvar Irrfan believed.
body:
• Meghna Gulzar told The Indian Express's Expresso series she had "nothing to do" directing Irrfan Khan in Talvar: "Everything he did, he made me look good."
  • She still doesn't know which of Talvar's competing perspectives Irrfan — who played investigator DCP Ashwin Kumar — believed.
  • On Vicky Kaushal, her Raazi and Sam Bahadur star: "I don't need to complete a sentence... that connection is just superb"; finding a bigger role than Sam Bahadur will be difficult.
  • On Deepika Padukone (Chhapaak): "She is a deep actor... She'll never stay on the surface." Her new film Daayra, starring Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran, releases September 18.

Meghna Gulzar has directed some of Hindi cinema's most exacting actors. But when The Indian Express's Expresso series asked her about Irrfan Khan, the Talvar director's answer was disarmingly simple: she had almost nothing to do.

The actor who needed no direction

"I really had nothing to do. Everything he did, he made me look good," Gulzar said of working with Irrfan Khan on Talvar, her 2015 drama based on the 2008 Aarushi Talwar murder case. The film, which presented the case through multiple battling perspectives, earned critical acclaim — including at the Toronto International Film Festival — and is widely regarded as one of the finest investigative dramas in Indian cinema.

"I really had nothing to do. Everything he did, he made me look good."

— Meghna Gulzar, on directing Irrfan Khan in Talvar

Irrfan, who died in 2020, played DCP Ashwin Kumar, the investigator at the story's centre. Gulzar revealed that one aspect of the collaboration still puzzles her. "I still don't know which side of Talvar's perspective he believes or agrees with," she said — a fitting coda for a film built on Rashomon-like ambiguity.

Vicky Kaushal and the unfinished sentence

Gulzar also discussed Vicky Kaushal, whom she directed in Raazi and Sam Bahadur, describing a working relationship that barely needs words. "I don't need to complete a sentence. He knows what I am going to say if I want him to do something differently. That connection is just superb," she said.

"I don't need to complete a sentence. He knows what I am going to say if I want him to do something differently. That connection is just superb."

— Meghna Gulzar, on Vicky Kaushal

She added that after Sam Bahadur, in which Kaushal played Field Marshal Sam Manekshaw, "it is going to be very difficult to find a role that is larger than that" — though the desire to work with him again is very much there.

Deepika and the others

On Deepika Padukone, who worked with her in Chhapaak, Gulzar said: "She is a deep actor. She'll never stay on the surface. She will go beneath the surface of the character, of the scene, of the story." She also joked about their similarities: "She's a bigger OCD than I am." The Expresso conversation ranged across the actors she has collaborated with over the years, including Alia Bhatt, Tabu, Sushmita Sen, Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran.

Daayra is next

Gulzar is currently preparing for the release of Daayra, which stars Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran and arrives in theatres on September 18, backed by Junglee Pictures and Pen Studios. In a separate interview with The Hollywood Reporter India, she said working with Prithviraj reminded her of Irrfan: "I honestly felt Irrfan sir would test me," she recalled. "You have to put your personal convictions aside, and start believing what the character is believing; that raises questions within you."

Six years after Irrfan's death, his shadow still falls across the directors he worked with — and Gulzar's Expresso interview is a reminder of why: an actor so complete that the director's best contribution was to get out of the way.
image_caption: Filmmaker Meghna Gulzar with Irrfan Khan. She directed him as investigator DCP Ashwin Kumar in Talvar.
nri_angle: For diaspora audiences who know Talvar and Raazi primarily through streaming, the Expresso conversation offers a rare window into how one of Hindi cinema's most restrained directors draws performances from its most demanding actors.
